 Swarm Defeat Capital City, 97-86, Behind Steinbach’s 28-Point Double-Double
 By Greensboro Swarm Staff / November 18, 2026
 Recap By: Kaitlyn Grenier 
 GREENSBORO, N.C. (Nov. 18, 2026) - The Greensboro Swarm (4-2), the NBA G League affiliate of the Charlotte Hornets, defeated the Capital City Go-Go (0-4), 97-86, in front of a sellout crowd on Wednesday at Novant Health Fieldhouse.
The Swarm had five different players score in double figures, including four of five starters. Hannes Steinbach led Greensboro with a 28-point, 16-rebound double-double on 13-of-15 shooting and added three steals and three blocked shots. Michael Ajayi also secured a double-double with 14 points, 13 rebounds, five assists and a steal. Kyle Mangas scored 12 points and Kylan Boswell scored 11 points, eight assists, and five rebounds. Off the bench, Josiah Allick added 10 points and six rebounds.
Steinbach became the sixth player in franchise history to reach 100 points in four games on Wednesday, while also reaching 71 rebounds in the stint.
Through his first four games with the Swarm, Steinbach has totaled 104 points and 71 rebounds, becoming the sixth player in franchise history to reach 100 points over that span. His 71 rebounds rank third-most in NBA G League history through a player's first four career games, and he is the only player in league history to record at least 100 points and 70 rebounds in his first four career games.
Greensboro opened the game strong, outscoring Capital City 30-23 in the first quarter. Mangas came out hot, scoring back-to-back 3-point shots to give the Swarm an early 6-2 lead. After the spurt, the Swarm allowed a 9-0 Capital City run, but it was cut short by a 3-point shot from Kobe Stewart. The Swarm continued scoring in the paint for the remainder of the quarter and shot 50% from the floor.
Capital City outscored the Swarm, 28-20, in the second quarter to take a one-point, 51-50, lead into halftime. Steinbach broke out during the second quarter with back-to-back shots at the rim to stop a Capital City run and force a timeout. Ajayi scored the last points in the second quarter for the Swarm with a dunk in this highly contested scoring contest.
After the half, Greensboro regained control of the game with a 23-18 frame to move ahead, 73-69, entering the fourth quarter. Steinbach started the third with three shots: a layup, dunk, and spinning jumper off an offensive rebound. He scored eight points again this quarter including another dunk that forced Capital City to call a timeout. 
The Swarm ended the game strong with a fourth-quarter margin of 24-17 to result in its win. Steinbach scored eight points for his third quarter in a row to close the game, putting in three dunks and forcing another Capital City timeout. Boswell also added five points, two assists, and a steal to secure the Swarm’s victory over the Capital City Go-Go.
With both sides shooting below 30% from distance, Greensboro took charge around the basket, leading 64-40 in the paint and winning the rebound battle, 51-36, while also generating 23 assists to Capital City’s 15.
Greensboro heads to Westchester to play the Knicks on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 7 p.m. ET.
